wanted_details.caution: According to the allegations in the indictment, the defendants conspired to participate in a multi-year fraudulent scheme to obtain remote IT work to generate revenue for the government of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. The scheme was allegedly carried out by facilitators in the United States who assisted others working on behalf of the DPRK to be hired as remote IT workers with U.S. companies, including by receiving and hosting laptop computers issued by victim companies at their residences. In total, the scheme impacted more than 70 U.S. company employers and generated approximately $3 million in revenue for IT workers, which is believed to have been sent to sanctioned entities controlled by the DPRK. An indictment is only a charge and is not evidence of guilt.

sources.title: DOJ charges 14 over a sprawling North Korean remote work scheme

disclaimer: Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo is a United States citizen, not a DPRK national, and is profiled here as a defendant charged as a domestic facilitator in a DPRK remote IT-worker scheme. The Justice Department names him, 37, of San Juan, Texas, among 14 defendants charged with wire fraud conspiracy, money laundering conspiracy, conspiracy to commit identity theft and aggravated identity theft, and states that he had recently been arrested and was expected to make an initial appearance in the Northern District of Ohio.

CyberScoop, reporting from the indictment, describes him as having hosted laptops at his home under various names and received about $190,000 from five employers; that description is the publication's and is cited to it.

The confidence level of 'confirmed' reflects that this individual is named in a federal indictment returned on 1 October 2026 and unsealed on 13 October 2026 in the Northern District of Ohio (United States v. Ming, 1:26-cr-00429); the conduct is alleged, and every person named is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law.
